editorial:
Fresh (2022) kicks off like a sweet rom-com but quickly turns into something much darker. You follow Noa, a woman tired of bad dating app matches, who meets a charming guy named Steve at the grocery store. Their chemistry feels real and fun, and you root for them right away. But the movie slowly pulls the rug out from under you, mixing horror, thriller, and dark comedy in a way that keeps you guessing. The vibe is playful at first, then tense and unsettling, with sharp humor sprinkled throughout. It is the kind of film that makes you laugh one minute and squirm the next.

The acting is strong, especially from the two leads, who make the wild story feel believable. The pacing is tight, and the movie never drags. The dark humor lands well, but the horror elements are genuinely disturbing, so this is not for the faint of heart. If you enjoy twisted thrillers with a sense of humor, you will have a great time.
endingExplained: In the final act, you learn Steve is a cannibal who sells human meat to wealthy clients. Noa discovers this and fights back, teaming up with her friend Mollie. They manage to escape after a brutal showdown, killing Steve and destroying his operation. The movie ends with Noa and Mollie walking away free, having survived the nightmare. It is a satisfying, bloody conclusion that rewards the tension built throughout.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves twisted thrillers with dark humor
